html:
SMTO-LLM-0013 — Model stream was malformed

GUID: 339606b3-515c-45e2-87b6-b19ff44cb956
Slug: llm-stream-protocol-error
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The pieces of the model's reply didn't fit together into one clear answer or action, or the model server reported an error partway through. SMTO didn't carry out any of it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. This small test shows whether the model server is answering normally right now.
  2. If the check passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). SMTO did not act on the broken reply, so trying the step again is safe and earlier finished steps are kept.
  3. If it keeps happening, choose another model in the Main card's Model field, select Save Main, and start the remaining work as a new task. Some models or servers send tool instructions in a layout SMTO can't safely piece together; a stopped task keeps its original model, so a new task is needed.

What success looks like

  • The task continues and the model's reply is accepted without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server. Before starting a new task, check what the stopped task already finished so nothing is done twice.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The native stream assembler could not combine the streamed events into one valid assistant response (a provider error event, a non-assistant role, malformed or ambiguous tool-call fragments, or an invalid finish reason).

What this means

  • The native stream assembler could not combine the events into one supported assistant decision. It validates roles, choice order, tool fragments and completion markers; a provider-reported error also enters this category. The bounded technical detail distinguishes these conditions. No root cause in the provider is established.

Why this can happen

  • An event violates the supported native response structure, or the provider explicitly reported a stream error.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the rejected field or event phase in Technical details. Have the provider operator check that case against a small native-tool test.

How to fix it

  • Read the error message and provider_diagnostic (stream_failure_stage, chunks_received, finish_reason) to see which check in NativeStreamAssembler.add or _add_call failed. Test the provider with a small native tool-call stream and fix its tool-call streaming format or serving configuration, or switch to a model with compatible native tool calling, then resume.
  • Have the provider operator check the rejected stream structure and tool format. Preserve the occurrence ID and test compatibility before another Agent decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The stream assembles into one complete validated assistant decision.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • reject attaches no_operation_authorized for this incomplete decision, not for previous operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
